name: Elam
title: Son of Shem and ancestor of the Elamites
summary: Elam was the eldest son of Shem, who was a son of Noah. He is regarded as the ancestor of the Elamites, an ancient people who lived in southwestern Iran. Elam is mentioned in the genealogy in Genesis and in several prophetic texts that speak of the fate of the Elamite people.

keyEvents.title: The birth and genealogy of Elam
keyEvents.description: Elam is mentioned as the firstborn son of Shem in the post-flood genealogy, as the ancestor of one of the great nations.

keyEvents.title: Repetition in the Genealogy of Shem
keyEvents.description: Elam is mentioned again in the detailed genealogy of Shem as the eldest of his five sons.

keyEvents.title: Kedorlaomer, King of Elam
keyEvents.description: King Kedorlaomer of Elam led a coalition of kings who ruled over the Valley of Sodom and was defeated by Abram, demonstrating the early military power of the Elamites.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy Against Elam
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah delivers prophecies where Elam is mentioned as part of God's plan for the nations, both as an instrument of judgment and as a recipient of judgment.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah's Judgment on Elam
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah pronounces a comprehensive prophecy of judgment against Elam, in which God says He will break Elam's bow and scatter the people, but also promises restoration in the last days.

keyEvents.title: Elamites Present on Pentecost Day
keyEvents.description: Elamites are mentioned among the nations present in Jerusalem on Pentecost day who heard the gospel preached in their own language, showing the continued existence of Elam's descendants.
